problem:
The vector-valued function $f(r,\theta ),$ given by

$$
f(r,\theta )=⟨4r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,\text{_____},\,{r}^{2}⟩
$$

parametrizes the elliptic paraboloid defined in Cartesian coordinates as 

$$
z=\frac{{x}^{2}}{16}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{3}.
$$

By first considering the transformations

$$
x=4X,\,y=\sqrt{3}Y,\,z=Z
$$

and writing the resulting system in cylindrical polar coordinates, determine the second component of $f.$
worked_solution:
First, substituting the transformations

$$
x=4X,\,y=\sqrt{3}Y,\,z=Z
$$

into our equation, we get

$$
Z={X}^{2}+{Y}^{2}.
$$

If $(r,\theta ,z)$ are the cylindrical coordinates of a point and $(X,Y,Z)$ are the corresponding Cartesian coordinates of that point, then we have

$$
X=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,Y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,Z=z.
$$

Substituting this into our equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}Z & ={X}^{2}+{Y}^{2} \\ Z & =(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}+(r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )^{2} \\ Z & ={r}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta ) \\ Z & ={r}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r,\theta ) & =⟨x,y,z⟩ \\  & =⟨4X,\sqrt{3}Y,Z⟩ \\  & =⟨4r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,\sqrt{3}r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,Z⟩ \\  & =⟨4r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,\sqrt{3}r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,{r}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $r\in [0,\infty )$ and $\theta \in [0,2\pi ).$

Therefore, the second component of $f$ is $\sqrt{3}r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .$
